title: Intrinsic magnetization of the superconducting condensate in Fe(Te,Se)
authors: M. J. Balakan, S. Heidari, G. Gu, Q. Li, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, J. U. Lee
figure_alt: Color map of magnetoresistance oscillations versus magnetic field and DC current in an Fe(Te,Se) ring, showing a current-dependent phase shift
summary: A superconductor whose Cooper pairs carry spin should be slightly magnetic on its own. In Fe(Te,Se) rings we detected that built-in magnetization: it shifts the phase of the superconducting quantum oscillations, grows linearly with the bias current, and changes direction in an unusual way with the current's polarity and size.
findings: An intrinsic magnetic field, encoded in the phase of Little–Parks oscillations, scales linearly with the DC bias current.
The magnetoresistance shows dual flux quantization: periodic in both the external magnetic field and the DC current.
A minimal model with Rashba coupling and an anisotropic out-of-plane interaction explains the data.
Evidence for spin-polarized superconductivity at the device scale, relevant to superconducting spintronics and quantum information.

title: Half-integer winding of order parameter in an iron-based superconductor
authors: M. J. Balakan, G. Gu, Q. Li, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, J. U. Lee
figure_alt: Normalized magnetoresistance maps versus winding number and DC current, showing oscillations at half the superconducting flux quantum
summary: In an ordinary superconducting ring the quantum phase winds by whole turns, so trapped magnetic flux comes in steps of h/2e. In a topological superconductor the phase can wind by half a turn. Phase-sensitive transport measurements on Fe(Te,Se) rings show quantum oscillations with half the usual flux period, the long-sought signature of half-integer winding.
findings: Superconducting quantum oscillations with a period of half the flux quantum, Φ₀/2.
The oscillations are modulated by a global current–field symmetry, consistent with strong spin–orbit coupling in the condensate.
Points toward non-Abelian excitations and scalable topological qubits.

cv.authors: M. J. Balakan, G. Gu, Q. Li, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, and J. U. Lee

title: Aharonov–Bohm interference from coherent spin-polarized edge transport in Fe(Te,Se) superconducting rings
authors: M. J. Balakan, S. Heidari, G. Gu, Q. Li, D. Titcombe, Z. Xiao, H. Frost, E. Bhatia, C. Kow, P. Rao, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, J. U. Lee
figure_alt: False-color scanning electron micrograph of a mesoscopic multi-ring Fe(Te,Se) device, scale bar 400 nm
summary: A topological superconductor should carry single electrons along its edges while its interior is superconducting. In Fe(Te,Se) rings we see both at once: an h/e interference signal from electrons travelling coherently along the edge, next to the h/2e signal of the superconducting bulk.
findings: Two periodicities in the magnetoresistance: h/e from ballistic edge interference and h/2e from fluxoid quantization of bulk Cooper pairs.
The Aharonov–Bohm oscillations appear only below the superconducting transition and show current–field symmetry.
Their temperature dependence follows a helical Luttinger liquid model, consistent with edge states of a topological superconductor.

cv.authors: M. J. Balakan, S. Heidari, G. Gu, Q. Li, D. Titcombe, Z. Xiao, H. Frost, E. Bhatia, C. Kow, P. Rao, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, and J. U. Lee

title: Observation of half-quantum vorticity in an iron-based superconductor
authors: M. J. Balakan, G. Gu, Q. Li, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, J. U. Lee
summary: Half-quantum vortices carry half the usual superconducting flux quantum and are predicted in superconductors whose Cooper pairs carry spin. Using mesoscopic ring devices of single-crystal Fe(Te,Se), a superconductor with helical Dirac surface states, we report direct transport signatures of half-quantum vorticity.
findings: Half-integer quantum oscillations arising from the splitting of quantized fluxoid states.
Distinct signatures of trapped half-integer fluxoids.
Oscillations modulated by a background symmetry set by the relative orientation of the DC bias current and the perpendicular magnetic field, consistent with strong spin–orbit coupling.
A step toward non-Abelian excitations in quantum materials and scalable topological qubits.

cv.authors: M. J. Balakan, G. Gu, Q. Li, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, and J. U. Lee

title: Chemical vapor deposition of two-dimensional boron sheets by thermal decomposition of diborane
authors: A. Mazaheri, M. Javadi, Y. Abdi
figure_alt: Borophene lattice model, layer-thickness histogram, and micrograph of borophene sheets next to aluminum domains
summary: Borophene, a one-atom-thick sheet of boron, is one of very few 2D metals and a candidate for ultrathin interconnects in future chips. Until this work it had been grown only by molecular beam epitaxy, which is slow and hard to scale. We grew it for the first time by chemical vapor deposition, using diborane gas as a pure boron source.
findings: First CVD growth of atomic-thickness borophene sheets.
Average thickness 4.2 Å, χ₃ crystal structure, metallic conductivity.
Evidence for stacked bilayer and trilayer borophene.
Systematic study of how temperature, deposition rate and pressure control growth.

cv.authors: A. Mazaheri, M. Javadi, and Y. Abdi

title: Kinetics of charge carriers across a graphene–silicon Schottky junction
authors: M. Javadi, A. Noroozi, Y. Abdi
summary: How fast can charge cross from a 2D sheet into a 3D crystal? Comparing graphene–silicon and gold–silicon contacts, we found that carriers cross the graphene interface about a million times more slowly, limited by how slowly electrons in graphene move out of its plane.
findings: Carrier transfer velocity across Au–Si is about 10⁷ cm/s, matching the thermal velocity in silicon.
Across graphene–Si it is about 10 cm/s, nearly six orders of magnitude smaller.
The effective out-of-plane velocity of carriers in graphene is about 1 cm/s.
Transfer velocity rises almost exponentially with Schottky barrier height, explained by T¹ scaling theory with barrier-dependent scattering.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, AA. Noroozi, and Y. Abdi

title: Theoretical efficiency limit of graphene–semiconductor solar cells
authors: M. Javadi
summary: A single-author calculation of the maximum power conversion efficiency of solar cells built from graphene on a conventional semiconductor, based on the scaling laws for thermionic emission across 2D/3D Schottky junctions.
findings: Under ideal conditions efficiency exceeds 25% for bandgaps between 1.1 and 1.7 eV.
Efficiency limits: 25.5% for graphene/silicon and 27.5% for graphene/GaAs.
Efficiency falls almost linearly with temperature: 0.076 %/K (graphene/Si) and 0.058 %/K (graphene/GaAs).

cv.authors: M. Javadi

title: Ultrahigh photovoltage responsivity of PEDOT:PSS–silicon hybrid heterojunction photodiodes
authors: A. H. Mosaddegh, A. A. Noroozi, M. Javadi, Y. Abdi
summary: Low-temperature, solution-processed polymer–silicon photodiodes that run without external power and stay stable after long storage in air.
findings: Self-powered photovoltage responsivity of 10⁶ V/W.
Noise-equivalent power of 10 pW/√Hz and detectivity up to 10¹⁰ Jones.
Thermal noise identified as the main limit on performance.

cv.authors: AH. Mosaddegh, AA. Noroozi, M. Javadi, and Y. Abdi

title: Sequentially assembled graphene layers on silicon, the role of uncertainty principles in graphene–silicon Schottky junctions
authors: M. Javadi, A. A. Noroozi, A. Mazaheri, Y. Abdi
figure_alt: Band diagram of the graphene–silicon interface and schematic of in-plane and out-of-plane current measurements
summary: Electrons in an atom-thin sheet barely move out of the sheet, so the uncertainty principle links a 2D layer's thickness to how easily charge enters the material beneath it. We stacked uncoupled CVD graphene layers one by one on silicon to test this on a macroscopic device.
findings: Sequentially assembled CVD graphene layers stay electronically uncoupled.
In-plane current scales with the number of assembled layers.
Layer thickness strongly modifies charge injection and the reverse saturation current of the graphene–silicon junction.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, AA. Noroozi, A. Mazaheri, Y. Abdi

title: Mechanism of charge transport in hybrid organic–inorganic PEDOT:PSS/silicon heterojunctions
authors: M. Javadi, A. Mazaheri, H. Torbatiyan, Y. Abdi
summary: Temperature- and voltage-dependent measurements show that current in polymer–silicon junctions follows different physics in each bias direction.
findings: Reverse bias: current is injection-limited by a quasi-Schottky barrier at the interface.
Forward bias: space-charge-limited current through the PEDOT:PSS layer, trap-limited at low bias.
Trap density about 5.6 × 10¹⁵ cm⁻³ with characteristic energy about 0.107 eV.
The double-logarithmic forward characteristic marks a transition from the Mark–Helfrich to the Mott–Gurney regime.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, A. Mazaheri, H. Torbatiyan, Y. Abdi

title: Frequency-driven bulk-to-surface transition of conductivity in ZnO nanowires
authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi
summary: The frequency of an applied AC voltage switches conduction in zinc oxide nanowires between the bulk and the surface.
findings: A continuous transition from positive to negative photoconductivity, centered at 48.9 kHz.
A frequency-driven metal–insulator transition at room temperature, near the same frequency.
A theory attributing both effects to switching between bulk and surface conduction.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi

title: Hybrid organic/inorganic position-sensitive detectors based on PEDOT:PSS/n-Si
authors: M. Javadi, M. Gholami, H. Torbatiyan, Y. Abdi
figure_alt: Schematic of the PEDOT:PSS on n-type silicon detector, optical transmittance of the polymer layers, and electron micrograph of the junction
figure_credit: Fig. 1(a–c) of the paper, © AIP Publishing
summary: A large-area optical sensor that reports where a light spot lands, made by coating silicon with a conductive polymer in a simple low-temperature process.
findings: Position sensitivity above 100 mV/mm.
Nonlinearity below 3% and response correlation above 0.995.
Response time under 4 ms for infrared illumination.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, M. Gholami, H. Torbatiyan, Y. Abdi

title: IR position-sensitive detectors based on double-junction asymmetric TiO₂/MoS₂/reduced graphene-oxide sandwiches
authors: M. Javadi, M. Gholami, Y. Abdi
summary: A self-powered infrared position sensor built from a stack of 2D MoS₂ grown by CVD on reduced graphene oxide, capped with TiO₂.
findings: Photocurrent sensitivity above 5000 nA/mm and photovoltage sensitivity above 20 mV/mm.
Nonlinearity below 1% and a correlation coefficient of 1.000 above 4 mW/cm².
Lateral photovoltage explained by the band alignment of the asymmetric stack.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, M. Gholami, Y. Abdi

title: Realization of enhanced sound-driven CNT-based triboelectric nanogenerator, utilizing sonic array configuration
authors: M. Javadi, A. Heidari, S. Darbari
summary: A sound-powered energy harvester whose output is boosted by placing it inside a cavity of steel slabs that traps the acoustic wave.
findings: Carbon nanotube electrodes increase the effective surface area.
A 1D phononic crystal of five steel slabs resonates near 4.3 kHz.
About 4× higher output voltage and 7× higher output power inside the sonic array.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, A. Heidari, S. Darbari

title: Ultra-low intensity UV detection using partitioned mesoporous TiO₂
authors: M. Javadi, H. Torbatiyan, Y. Abdi
summary: Dividing a porous TiO₂ film into narrow partitions makes it detect very faint ultraviolet light about 100,000 times better.
findings: Five orders of magnitude enhancement in ultra-low-intensity UV detection.
Responsivity of about 0.1 A/W at 100 µW/cm² and 0.01 A/W at 14 µW/cm².
The partitioned film behaves as a quasi-one-dimensional transport medium.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, H. Torbatiyan, Y. Abdi

title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of single-electron multiple-trapping transport in disordered media
authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi
summary: A simulation method for electron transport in disordered semiconductors that stays accurate even when disorder is strong.
findings: Uses the full density of localized states instead of a truncated one.
Adds an occupation index to account for filled trap sites.
Validated across a broad range of disorder, Fermi level and temperature.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi

title: Nanopattern formation using localized plasma for growth of single-standing carbon nanotubes
authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi
summary: A plasma-based method that makes carbon nanotubes grow as self-organized, individually standing patterns.
findings: The plasma localizes around the growth region and exerts a dielectrophoretic force on the nickel catalyst.
Numerical simulations of the localized plasma reproduce the observed patterns.
A low-cost route to nanotube arrays for photonic crystals and field-emission devices.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi

title: Electron transport in Q2D porous network of titania nanoparticles, incorporating electrical and optical advantages in dye-sensitized solar cells
authors: M. Javadi, S. Alizadeh, Y. Khosravi, Y. Abdi
figure_alt: Electron micrographs of a micro-patterned porous TiO₂ layer in top and cross-section views
summary: Shaping a solar cell's porous TiO₂ layer into micro-scale walls guides electrons toward the collecting electrode.
findings: Electron diffusion coefficient about ten times higher than in a conventional porous layer at high Fermi levels.
About three times longer electron diffusion length.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, S. Alizadeh, Y. Khosravi, Y. Abdi

title: Realization of a piezo-phototronic device based on reduced graphene-oxide/MoS₂ heterostructure
authors: M. Javadi, S. Darbari, Y. Abdi, F. Ghasemi
summary: A flexible photodetector whose response to light improves when it is bent, combining semiconducting, piezoelectric MoS₂ with graphene oxide.
findings: MoS₂ raises photoresponsivity about 2.1× at 450 nm compared with graphene oxide alone.
About 97% responsivity enhancement under combined illumination and 0.03% strain.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, S. Darbari, Y. Abdi, F. Ghasemi

title: Local collection efficiency in nano-crystalline solar cells
authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi, E. Arzi
summary: A geometrical model, based on the random nature of diffusion, for how efficiently a nanocrystalline solar cell collects electrons generated at each depth.
findings: Derives a general form of the total collection efficiency, η = 1 − τ(IMPS)/τ(IMVS), valid for any solar cell.
Proposes a direct way to estimate the electron diffusion length from IMPS and IMVS measurements.

cv.authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi, E. Arzi

title: Enhancing the electron lifetime and diffusion coefficient in dye-sensitized solar cells by patterning the layer of titanium dioxide nanoparticles
authors: M. Sajedi Alvar, M. Javadi, Y. Abdi, E. Arzi
summary: A micro-patterned TiO₂ anode gives dye-sensitized solar cells faster electron transport and less recombination.
findings: Patterning the nanoparticle layer increases both electron lifetime and diffusion coefficient.

cv.authors: M. Sajedi Alvar, M. Javadi, Y. Abdi, E. Arzi

title: Monte Carlo random walk simulation of electron transport in confined porous TiO₂ as a promising candidate for photo-electrode of nano-crystalline solar cells
authors: M. Javadi, Y. Abdi
summary: Simulations showing that confining porous TiO₂ into columns, instead of a thick uniform layer, steers electron diffusion toward the electrode.
findings: Continuous-time random walk simulation of electron transport in porous TiO₂.
Structural confinement induces directional diffusion, a route to higher internal quantum efficiency.
